data.description:
## Context
After family cutovers, reachable generic retry, `_best_effort` swallowing, duck-typed dispatch, or duplicate SDK/adapter retry would preserve the original failure class and invite future bypass.

## Outcome
Prove every supported Cloud/DC mutation has exactly one typed coordinator/adapter owner, remove obsolete production fallbacks, and fail unsupported live actions before any effect.

## Plan
1. Build a dispatch census over every `MutationDirection`/`MutationAction` and Cloud/DC provider route. Require one typed owner or an intentional provider-neutral pre-effect unsupported result.
2. Remove generic whole-operation retry, `_best_effort` write swallowing, production class-name/duck fallbacks, and duplicate SDK/adapter retry owners after their route is covered.
3. Keep compatibility only at serialized/public read boundaries; tests use explicit protocol fakes.
4. Add static/string and runtime poison tests that fail when removed helpers remain reachable from production.
5. Preserve rollback as code/routing reversion plus remote re-observation; never compensate by deleting successful Jira work.

## Testing
The census must fail on missing, duplicate, or fallback owners. Effect spies prove unsupported actions fail before local/remote writes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every supported Cloud/DC mutation route has exactly one typed coordinator/adapter owner.
- [ ] Unsupported production actions return a typed provider-neutral error before any effect.
- [ ] Generic whole-operation retry and `_best_effort` write swallowing are unreachable from production.
- [ ] Production class-name/duck dispatch and duplicate SDK/adapter retry owners are unreachable.
- [ ] Tests use explicit declared protocols rather than production fallback paths.
- [ ] Rollback guidance requires re-observation and never remote deletion.

## Out of scope
Final output contracts, state advancement, end-to-end validation, and docs.
data.title: RP-03 S5 T1 — Census typed routes and remove legacy write fallbacks
